title: Proverbs, Chapter 12 (Leningrad Codex)
source: Leningrad Codex folios (Internet Archive, WSRP photographs) + tanach.us LC folio index + UXLC Hebrew + KJV
description: Proverbs 12 on folios 413v, 414r of the Leningrad Codex (1008 AD), the oldest complete Hebrew Bible. Hebrew from the UXLC transcription of this manuscript; English KJV.
introduction:
Proverbs chapter 12 from the Leningrad Codex (Codex Leningradensis, National Library of Russia, Firkovich EBP. I B 19a), copied in Cairo by Samuel ben Jacob and dated 1008/1009 AD, the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible and the base text of the Biblia Hebraica editions. This chapter stands on folios 413v, 414r.

This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side(s) carrying each section's verses, from the full-colour West Semitic Research Project photographs of the codex as redistributed on Internet Archive (item Leningrad_Codex_Color_Images, marked Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0). Folio-to-verse ranges come from the tanach.us LC folio index, which was derived from the West Semitic Research Project's published index; each section links only to the page(s) whose recorded verse range contains its verses.
  2. Original text: the verbatim Hebrew of this manuscript in the Unicode/XML Leningrad Codex (UXLC 2.5 build 27.6, tanach.us), a transcription of Firkovich B 19a with vowels and cantillation, released without restriction on the biblical text.
  3. English translation: the King James Version (1611, public domain), retrieved verbatim from bolls.life (KJV text, Strong's numbers stripped).
translator_notes: Ketiv/Qere: where the scribe wrote one form (ketiv) but the Masoretes read another (qere), the consonantal ketiv is given first and the vocalised qere follows in square brackets. פ and ס mark the open and closed paragraph breaks visible as gaps in the manuscript columns.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>אֹהֵ֣ב מ֖וּסָר אֹ֣הֵֽב דָּ֑עַת וְשֹׂנֵ֖א תוֹכַ֣חַת בָּֽעַר׃ <sup>2</sup>ט֗וֹב יָפִ֣יק רָ֭צוֹן מֵיְהוָ֑ה וְאִ֖ישׁ מְזִמּ֣וֹת יַרְשִֽׁיעַ׃ <sup>3</sup>לֹא־יִכּ֣וֹן אָדָ֣ם בְּרֶ֑שַׁע וְשֹׁ֥רֶשׁ צַ֝דִּיקִ֗ים בַּל־יִמּֽוֹט׃ <sup>4</sup>אֵֽשֶׁת־חַ֭יִל עֲטֶ֣רֶת בַּעְלָ֑הּ וּכְרָקָ֖ב בְּעַצְמוֹתָ֣יו מְבִישָֽׁה׃ <sup>5</sup>מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת צַדִּיקִ֣ים מִשְׁפָּ֑ט תַּחְבֻּל֖וֹת רְשָׁעִ֣ים מִרְמָֽה׃ <sup>6</sup>דִּבְרֵ֣י רְשָׁעִ֣ים אֱרָב־דָּ֑ם וּפִ֥י יְ֝שָׁרִ֗ים יַצִּילֵֽם׃ <sup>7</sup>הָפ֣וֹךְ רְשָׁעִ֣ים וְאֵינָ֑ם וּבֵ֖ית צַדִּיקִ֣ים יַעֲמֹֽד׃ <sup>8</sup>לְֽפִי־שִׂ֭כְלוֹ יְהֻלַּל־אִ֑ישׁ וְנַעֲוֵה־לֵ֝֗ב יִהְיֶ֥ה לָבֽוּז׃
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>Whoso loveth instruction loveth knowledge: but he that hateth reproof is brutish. <sup>2</sup>A good man obtaineth favour of the LORD: but a man of wicked devices will he condemn. <sup>3</sup>A man shall not be established by wickedness: but the root of the righteous shall not be moved. <sup>4</sup>A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband: but she that maketh ashamed is as rottenness in his bones. <sup>5</sup>The thoughts of the righteous are right: but the counsels of the wicked are deceit. <sup>6</sup>The words of the wicked are to lie in wait for blood: but the mouth of the upright shall deliver them. <sup>7</sup>The wicked are overthrown, and are not: but the house of the righteous shall stand. <sup>8</sup>A man shall be commended according to his wisdom: but he that is of a perverse heart shall be despised.

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>ט֣וֹב נִ֭קְלֶה וְעֶ֣בֶד ל֑וֹ מִ֝מְּתַכַּבֵּ֗ד וַחֲסַר־לָֽחֶם׃ <sup>10</sup>יוֹדֵ֣עַ צַ֭דִּיק נֶ֣פֶשׁ בְּהֶמְתּ֑וֹ וְֽרַחֲמֵ֥י רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים אַכְזָרֽ͏ִי׃ <sup>11</sup>עֹבֵ֣ד אַ֭דְמָתוֹ יִֽשְׂבַּֽע־לָ֑חֶם וּמְרַדֵּ֖ף רֵיקִ֣ים חֲסַר־לֵֽב׃ <sup>12</sup>חָמַ֣ד רָ֭שָׁע מְצ֣וֹד רָעִ֑ים וְשֹׁ֖רֶשׁ צַדִּיקִ֣ים יִתֵּֽן׃ <sup>13</sup>בְּפֶ֣שַׁע שְׂ֭פָתַיִם מוֹקֵ֣שׁ רָ֑ע וַיֵּצֵ֖א מִצָּרָ֣ה צַדִּֽיק׃ <sup>14</sup>מִפְּרִ֣י פִי־אִ֭ישׁ יִשְׂבַּע־ט֑וֹב וּגְמ֥וּל יְדֵי־אָ֝דָ֗ם ישוב [יָשִׁ֥יב] לֽוֹ׃ <sup>15</sup>דֶּ֣רֶךְ אֱ֭וִיל יָשָׁ֣ר בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְשֹׁמֵ֖עַ לְעֵצָ֣ה חָכָֽם׃ <sup>16</sup>אֱוִ֗יל בַּ֭יּוֹם יִוָּדַ֣ע כַּעְס֑וֹ וְכֹסֶ֖ה קָל֣וֹן עָרֽוּם׃
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>He that is despised, and hath a servant, is better than he that honoureth himself, and lacketh bread. <sup>10</sup>A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast: but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel. <sup>11</sup>He that tilleth his land shall be satisfied with bread: but he that followeth vain persons is void of understanding. <sup>12</sup>The wicked desireth the net of evil men: but the root of the righteous yieldeth fruit. <sup>13</sup>The wicked is snared by the transgression of his lips: but the just shall come out of trouble. <sup>14</sup>A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth: and the recompence of a man's hands shall be rendered unto him. <sup>15</sup>The way of a fool is right in his own eyes: but he that hearkeneth unto counsel is wise. <sup>16</sup>A fool's wrath is presently known: but a prudent man covereth shame.

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>יָפִ֣יחַ אֱ֭מוּנָה יַגִּ֣יד צֶ֑דֶק וְעֵ֖ד שְׁקָרִ֣ים מִרְמָֽה׃ <sup>18</sup>יֵ֣שׁ בּ֖וֹטֶה כְּמַדְקְר֣וֹת חָ֑רֶב וּלְשׁ֖וֹן חֲכָמִ֣ים מַרְפֵּֽא׃ <sup>19</sup>שְֽׂפַת־אֱ֭מֶת תִּכּ֣וֹן לָעַ֑ד וְעַד־אַ֝רְגִּ֗יעָה לְשׁ֣וֹן שָֽׁקֶר׃ <sup>20</sup>מִ֭רְמָה בְּלֶב־חֹ֣רְשֵׁי רָ֑ע וּֽלְיֹעֲצֵ֖י שָׁל֣וֹם שִׂמְחָֽה׃ <sup>21</sup>לֹא־יְאֻנֶּ֣ה לַצַּדִּ֣יק כָּל־אָ֑וֶן וּ֝רְשָׁעִ֗ים מָ֣לְאוּ רָֽע׃ <sup>22</sup>תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה שִׂפְתֵי־שָׁ֑קֶר וְעֹשֵׂ֖י אֱמוּנָ֣ה רְצוֹנֽוֹ׃ <sup>23</sup>אָדָ֣ם עָ֭רוּם כֹּ֣סֶה דָּ֑עַת וְלֵ֥ב כְּ֝סִילִ֗ים יִקְרָ֥א אִוֶּֽלֶת׃ <sup>24</sup>יַד־חָרוּצִ֥ים תִּמְשׁ֑וֹל ו֝רְמִיָּ֗ה תִּהְיֶ֥ה לָמַֽס׃
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>He that speaketh truth sheweth forth righteousness: but a false witness deceit. <sup>18</sup>There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health. <sup>19</sup>The lip of truth shall be established for ever: but a lying tongue is but for a moment. <sup>20</sup>Deceit is in the heart of them that imagine evil: but to the counsellors of peace is joy. <sup>21</sup>There shall no evil happen to the just: but the wicked shall be filled with mischief. <sup>22</sup>Lying lips are abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly are his delight. <sup>23</sup>A prudent man concealeth knowledge: but the heart of fools proclaimeth foolishness. <sup>24</sup>The hand of the diligent shall bear rule: but the slothful shall be under tribute.

translation.original_text: <sup>25</sup>דְּאָגָ֣ה בְלֶב־אִ֣ישׁ יַשְׁחֶ֑נָּה וְדָבָ֖ר ט֣וֹב יְשַׂמְּחֶֽנָּה׃ <sup>26</sup>יָתֵ֣ר מֵרֵעֵ֣הוּ צַדִּ֑יק וְדֶ֖רֶךְ רְשָׁעִ֣ים תַּתְעֵֽם׃ <sup>27</sup>לֹא־יַחֲרֹ֣ךְ רְמִיָּ֣ה צֵיד֑וֹ וְהוֹן־אָדָ֖ם יָקָ֣ר חָרֽוּץ׃ <sup>28</sup>בְּאֹֽרַח־צְדָקָ֥ה חַיִּ֑ים וְדֶ֖רֶךְ נְתִיבָ֣ה אַל־מָֽוֶת׃
translation.text: <sup>25</sup>Heaviness in the heart of man maketh it stoop: but a good word maketh it glad. <sup>26</sup>The righteous is more excellent than his neighbour: but the way of the wicked seduceth them. <sup>27</sup>The slothful man roasteth not that which he took in hunting: but the substance of a diligent man is precious. <sup>28</sup>In the way of righteousness is life; and in the pathway thereof there is no death.
